text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.

- The National Radio and Television Council (KRRiT) granted two new concessions for private television stations. They went to Nasza Telewizja, owned by a group of Polish businessmen, and to TVN belonging to Mariusz Walter.

- According to experts of the Foundation of Assistance Programmes for Agriculture, only a third of Poland's two million farms earn reasonable incomes, invest and stand a chance of competing with farms of West Europe. The technology most use is at the same level as the EU in the 1960s.
- PKO BP bank will lower annual interest paid on checking accounts to 12.5 percent from 13 percent, from March 1.
- Probably the first subsidiary Rolimpex will introduce on the stock exchange will be feed producer Dobropasz. This year a non-public issue nominally valued at 10-12 million zlotys is planned.

- Research by the economic development institute of the Higher Trade School in Warsaw shows that after the positive climate in construction in the final quarter of last year, the index fell 25 points to minus 7.1 points.
- Large concerns have invested $500 million to date in Poland's telecommunications network, according to the State Foreign Investment Agency PAIZ.
- The Tarnow-based company Ampli, a wholesaler of electrical equipment, plans to issue shares to the public and be quoted on the bourse's new free market.
- The managment of Pekao SA neither confirmed nor denied reports that BudBank will soon enter the banking group headed by Pekao.
- Canada's Hariston Corporation has sold a million shares of Polish Life Improvement (PLI).
